subStrands.name: Farm Animals — Importance, Classification and Body Systems

objectives.description: Importance of farm animals: source of food (meat, milk, eggs, honey etc); raw materials e.g. hide and skin, bones, hooves, hair/fur, egg shells; source of manure (fertilizer, biogas, bio fuel); animal power (animal traction, transportation); research (laboratory, field), drugs, vaccines, hormones etc; source of employment; social functions; for security; as pets; sports and games; religious festivals; source of foreign exchange through export of animal products and by-products.

Classification of farm animals based on stomach type: Simple stomach (non-ruminant or monogastric) e.g. poultry (avian), pig (swine), rabbits, horses, donkeys, snails, bees, grasscutters; Complex stomach (polygastric or ruminants) i.e. cattle, sheep and goat.
Identification of ruminants and non-ruminants based on external features, type of stomach and type of feed consumed.

Internal organs and their functions in farm animals: identification of internal organs e.g. liver, lungs, heart, kidney, spleen, pancreas, stomach, crop, caecum, gizzard, small intestine, large intestine, tongue etc, and their functions.
Body systems and their functions in farm animals: digestive, respiratory, nervous, circulatory, skeletal, reproductive systems.

Definition of terms used in livestock reproduction: ovulation, oestrus cycle, heat period, signs of heat, mating, gestation, parturition, lactation, colostrum, flushing, steaming up, dystocia, vaginal prolapse etc.
Reproduction in livestock (mammals): detection of heat, mating systems, pregnancy detection and signs of parturition.
Reproduction in poultry: process of egg formation in poultry.
Reproductive hormones and their functions: sources and roles of female hormones (oestrogen, progesterone, relaxin, oxytocin etc) and male hormones (testosterone/androgen).

Management of pregnant farm animals: regular and adequate feeding, body exercise, steaming up, separation from male animals, provision of clean and adequate water and administration of drugs where necessary, dipping to eliminate ecto-parasites, parturition etc.
Livestock management systems: intensive, semi-intensive and extensive system — advantages and disadvantages of each of the systems.

Management practices of livestock: housing requirements for farm animals; management practices including feeding, sanitation, hygiene, castration, dehorning, deworming, vaccination, inoculation, culling, debeaking, smoking (in bees), docking, means of identification of farm animals (tattooing, branding, ear-notching, rings etc), isolation, weaning, care of the young animal until weaned; simple record keeping; management practices from birth to maturity of a named large ruminant, small ruminant, poultry, pigs, grasscutter, bees and snails.

Meaning and classes of animal feeds: meaning of animal nutrition, feed nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats and oil, vitamins, minerals and water), their functions, sources and deficiencies in farm animals; classification of animal feeds into concentrates, roughages, supplements, feed additives etc.

Livestock rations: meaning of livestock rations and types (balanced, maintenance, production rations); malnutrition — meaning, causes, symptoms and practical ways to check malnutrition such as feeding balanced rations, feeding weaker animals separately, deworming, giving supplementary feeds, addition of feed additives to stimulate appetite, protecting animals from toxic plants and harmful substances, adjusting stocking rates, provision of good quality and adequate water.

Formulation of livestock rations: practical diet formulations for the different classes of farm animals (starter, grower and finisher diets); identification of different feed ingredients used for diet formulations e.g. blood meal, fish meal, cotton seed cake, oyster shell, groundnut cake, maize grains, salt, premix, glycine etc; factors to consider in feed formulation e.g. physiological status of animal, species, age, body weight, production target, acceptability of feed, nutrient composition, ingredient availability, cost of feed ingredients.

Processing techniques for different farm animal products: pre-slaughtering, slaughtering and post-slaughtering activities; hygienic conditions in processing; slaughtering techniques for different farm animals; processing of animal products e.g. egg, milk, meat, skin, wool, honey, snail shell and feathers, fur, hooves, horns, blood, faeces/droppings into other forms (value addition).
Marketing of animal products: common marketing channels and agents such as producers, wholesalers, retailers, consumers etc; advantages and disadvantages of each marketing channel and agent.
Meaning and importance of pasture and forage crops: definition, examples and importance of pasture and forage crops.
Types of pasture and forage crops: types and features of pasture and forage crops.
Terminologies in pasture management: basic terminologies in pasture management.
Meaning and characteristics of rangelands: meaning and features of rangeland.
Methods of rangeland improvement: reseeding, rotational grazing, controlled stocking, deferred grazing, controlled burning, fertilizer application, pest control, disease control etc.
Importance of rangeland in livestock production: provision of vegetable and grasses for animals, exercise, provision of hay and silage etc.
Meaning of animal improvement and terminologies used in animal improvement.

Aims/importance of farm animal improvement: high reproductive efficiency, potency, mothering ability, cool temperament, high libido, resistance to pests, resistance to diseases, tolerance to harsh environment, etc.
Methods used in farm animal improvement: introduction, selection and breeding — merits and demerits of each method.
Artificial insemination: meaning, methods (identification of materials, methods, steps and precautions), and advantages of artificial insemination.
Concept of farm animal disease: meaning and causal agents (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa) of diseases in farm animals.

General symptoms of diseases in farm animals: loss of appetite, loss of weight, diarrhoea, high body temperature, blood stained urine, gnashing of teeth, discharges from natural openings, blood stained faeces, ruffled feathers or fur, standing hair, undue noise, excessive salivation, anaemia, staggering gait, difficulty in breathing, coma, sudden death etc.

Diseases of farm animals, prevention and control: identification of the main diseases of farm animals, their causal agents, mode of transmission and symptoms; simple preventive and control measures including the use of antibiotics and ethno veterinary practices.
Factors predisposing farm animals to diseases: poor nutrition, poor health status, poor sanitation, inadequate bio security, overcrowding, unfavourable weather conditions, low immunity etc.

Livestock parasites: meaning, classes, control/prevention and effects of parasites on farm animals; life cycles of the parasites; identification and economic importance of ecto-parasites (ticks, lice, mites, fleas etc.) and endo-parasites (tapeworm, roundworm, hookworm, pinworm, liver fluke, trypanosome etc).

Livestock pests: knowledge of livestock pests (rodents, snakes, soldier ants, birds, weevils, termites, flies etc), prevention/control using dewormers, acaricides, pesticides and ethno veterinary practices, and effects of pests on farm animals; economic importance of storage pests (rodents, weevils, termites, cockroaches etc) and field pests (soldier ants, birds, snakes, flies etc).

Products and by-products of farm animals: identification and uses of animal products and by-products such as meat, eggs, milk, honey, hides, skin, blood, hair, wool, feathers, horn, hooves, bones, snail shell, animal dung etc.
Identification of farm animals: ability to describe, draw and label the external parts of farm animals.

Internal organs and their functions in farm animals: identification and drawing of major internal structures in the various body systems of a named ruminant, poultry and pig; differences in structures and their functions.

Tools and equipment used in management of farm animals: identification of tools and equipment used in housing, brooding, feeding, identification, debeaking, castration, handling, dehorning, incubation, milking, slaughtering, pasture and forage crop management.

Feeds and feedstuffs: identification and uses of common feed ingredients (maize, groundnut cake, soya bean meal, palm kernel cake, fish meal, bone meal, oyster shell, limestone, salt, salt lick, premix, wheat offal etc), crop residues, agricultural by-products and non-conventional feeds.
Pasture and forage crops: identification and uses of common pasture and forage crops; hay and silage making.
Artificial insemination: identification of tools and equipment and their uses; simple techniques of semen collection, preservation and insemination.
Pests of farm animals: identification and economic importance of storage pests (rodents, weevils, termites, cockroaches etc) and field pests (soldier ants, birds, snakes, flies etc).

Parasites of farm animals: identification and economic importance of ectoparasites (ticks, lice, mites, fleas etc) and endoparasites (tapeworm, roundworms, hookworm, pinworm, liver fluke, trypanosomes etc); life cycles, prevention and control of these parasites.
